subject: SOC 2 gaps & acceptance matrix — BrightBank scope alignment
messages:
From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai>
To: Jacob Reed <jacob.reed@brightbank.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 30 Sep 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: SOC 2 gaps & acceptance matrix — BrightBank scope alignment

Hi Jacob — thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our call plus the concrete asks we discussed so we can keep momentum.

Summary of what we heard from BrightBank
- Primary goal: adopt Redwood for production inference while preserving current audit/compliance posture (SOC 2 + internal audit).
- Top pain points: (1) proof of audit-log completeness and retention controls, (2) DPA language around processor/subprocessor stacks, and (3) pen-test evidence / vulnerability management cadence.
- Desired timeline: security sign-off for a pilot by mid-November; procurement/legal to follow.

Items we (Redwood) committed to deliver this week
1) A control-gap matrix mapping BrightBank SOC 2 control areas to Redwood evidence artifacts and mitigations (see attached SOC2_Control_GapMatrix_BrightBank.xlsx).
2) A redacted sample of our audit logs showing event types, retention metadata, and export format (audit_log_sample_events.json).
3) A draft DPA with the specific retention, subprocessor, and incident-notification language you requested (DPA_Draft_BrightBank.docx).
4) A one-page summary of recent external pen test outcomes with remediation status (pen_test_summary_redacted.pdf).

Clarifying Qs / asks for BrightBank
- Can you confirm which BrightBank control families we should prioritize in the matrix (e.g., CC6/CC7 vs CC3)? That will shape the level of evidence we assemble.
- Who from your internal audit team will be the primary reviewer and what format do they prefer (spreadsheet vs. portal access)?

Next steps / timeline
- I will send the artifacts listed above by EOD Friday (this week).
- Neha will be your technical lead for log-format / retention follow-ups; Laura will own legal/DPA items; Marcus will handle penetration-testing background and remediation summaries.
- Jacob to confirm pilot scope & primary auditors by 10/6.

Thanks — very doable, and we want this to be as narrow as possible for pilot sign-off.

Best,
Sergio Alvarez
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0178

Attachments: SOC2_Control_GapMatrix_BrightBank.xlsx; audit_log_sample_events.json; DPA_Draft_BrightBank.docx; pen_test_summary_redacted.pdf

From: Jacob Reed <jacob.reed@brightbank.com>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai>
Cc: BrightBank Security Team <security@brightbank.com>, Elaine Park <elaine.park@brightbank.com>
Date: Fri, 1 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0400
Subject: Re: SOC 2 gaps & acceptance matrix — BrightBank scope alignment

Sergio — thanks for the detailed recap and for pulling the team together. Quick notes from our side: 

1) Priority controls: focus first on CC6 (system operations & logging), CC7 (change management), and CC3 (data protection). If you can map artifacts to those three, that will cover our internal audit drive.
2) Primary reviewer: Elaine Park (copied) from Internal Audit — spreadsheet preferred, and we like a column for "what evidence looks like" + a link to the artifact.
3) On pen testing: we will need your high-level timeline for third-party pen tests and confirmation that results can be redacted for vendor review.

We look forward to the artifacts. Small ask: can you include an example log retention policy that shows retention periods per event type? That will help legal.

-Jacob
Jacob Reed
Director, Infrastructure Security | BrightBank
jacob.reed@brightbank.com | (202) 555-0112

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Jacob Reed <jacob.reed@brightbank.com>, BrightBank Security Team <security@brightbank.com>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 1 Oct 2026 11:46:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SOC 2 gaps & acceptance matrix — BrightBank scope alignment

Hi Jacob / BrightBank team — attaching the artifacts Sergio mentioned and adding a short technical note below. Attachments: SOC2_Control_GapMatrix_BrightBank.xlsx (tabbed by control family), audit_log_sample_events.json (sample export, truncated), DPA_Draft_BrightBank.docx, pen_test_summary_redacted.pdf.

Technical notes (summary):
- Audit logs: export demonstrates event types (auth, model_call, admin_change), timestamps in RFC3339, user_id / request_id correlation keys, and a retention flag. We currently retain auth and admin_change events for 3 years; model_call token-level logs are retained for 90 days by default but can be extended for enterprise pilots with contractual retention.
- Retention controls: retention is implemented at the object-store policy level with immutable retention windows + scheduled lifecycle rules.
- Subprocessors & DPA: the DPA draft includes our subprocessors list and a proposed 30/60/90 SLA ladder for incident notification. We can negotiate exact retention/erasure language for pilot customers in the DPA exhibit.
- Pen test evidence: attached PDF is redacted to remove customer-identifying artifacts; it includes test scope, CVSS summary, and remediation status for high/critical findings (most are closed or scheduled).

Open items for BrightBank to confirm:
- Desired retention for model_call logs for the pilot (90 / 180 / 365 days).
- Whether you need continuous access to the raw audit stream (S3 push) or periodic exports (weekly).

If it helps, we can set a short working session next week (30 minutes) to walk the matrix with Elaine and the audit team.

-Neha
Neha Kapoor
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwood.ai | +1 (650) 555-0233

Attachments: SOC2_Control_GapMatrix_BrightBank.xlsx; audit_log_sample_events.json; DPA_Draft_BrightBank.docx; pen_test_summary_redacted.pdf

From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai>
To: Jacob Reed <jacob.reed@brightbank.com>, Elaine Park <elaine.park@brightbank.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 2 Oct 2026 11:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SOC 2 gaps & acceptance matrix — BrightBank scope alignment

Thanks for the confirmation, Jacob and Elaine. Quick answers and proposed next steps: 

- Retention default for pilot: propose 180 days for model_call logs (we'll reflect in the DPA exhibit) unless you expressly need 365 — option to extend in pilot SOW.
- Export mode: recommend S3 push for continuous streaming of audit events (we can set up a separate read-only bucket for auditors). If your auditors prefer periodic exports, we can schedule weekly full exports as a backup.
- Pen test: we can provide signed redacted reports and a remediation timeline; Marcus will coordinate scope questions and provide a short note on our current cadence (quarterly internal + annual third-party).

Proposed next steps:
1) Elaine/Internal Audit — please review the attached matrix by 10/6 and mark any "must-have" controls.
2) Redwood: update DPA exhibit to show 180-day pilot retention and provide S3 export instructions by 10/8.
3) Schedule a 30-min working review with Elaine + Neha the week of 10/11 — I'll send calendar invites once Elaine confirms availability.

If that all sounds good I'll move the documents into a read-only share and send the HubSpot record link for tracking.

Best regards,
Sergio Alvarez
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0178

Attachments: SOC2_Control_GapMatrix_BrightBank.xlsx; DPA_Draft_BrightBank.docx
